description:
Batch video and audio shrinker for Windows - encodes on your GPU with the codecs Windows already has, no FFmpeg and no uploads.

DownSample shrinks videos and audio to save disk space — without FFmpeg and without uploading anything. It drives Windows Media Foundation — the OS's own licensed H.264 / AAC — and encodes on your GPU's hardware blocks (NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel iGPU) via Direct3D 11. Drop in files or a whole folder, pick a target height (4K down to 240p or custom), aspect ratio, quality, and audio bitrate, then shrink the entire queue in parallel across every CPU and GPU you have. Preview your settings on a single file first, keep or replace originals, and add a name suffix. No bundled codec, no network, no telemetry — your media never leaves the machine.

Free for personal use; business or commercial use requires a paid license.

- Same font and text sizes as the other TAPATCH apps, so most text is a little bigger
- New UI size in Settings → Size and window: text, buttons and panels get bigger or smaller together (60–200%). Ctrl + and Ctrl − work too, Ctrl 0 goes back to 100%
- The window opens where you left it, on the same screen and at the same size. Or pick Full screen under When the window opens
- The savings tag in the file list no longer overlaps the new file size
